solution: Coefficient determinant: \(\begin{vmatrix}1&2&3\\2&1&3\\5&5&9\end{vmatrix}=1(9-15)-2(18-15)+3(10-5)=-6-6+15=3\). Since \(\Delta=3\neq0\), by Cramer's rule the system has a UNIQUE solution. Solving: \(R_2\to R_2-2R_1\) gives \(-3y-3z=0\Rightarrow y=-z\); \(R_3\to R_3-5R_1\) gives \(-5y-6z=-1\). Substituting \(y=-z\): \(5z-6z=-1\Rightarrow z=1\), so \(y=-1\) and \(x=1-2(-1)-3(1)=0\). The unique solution is \((x,y,z)=(0,-1,1)\), which satisfies all three equations. Hence (A). [Note: an earlier version of this solution row-reduced correctly but then mis-stated the rank as 2; the two reduced rows are independent, so the rank is 3 and the solution is unique.]

\(f(x)=2\cos^2x-1=\cos 2x\), so \(f'(x)=-2\sin 2x\). The function decreases where \(f'(x)<0\), i.e. where \(\sin 2x>0\), i.e. \(2x\in(2k\pi,\,2k\pi+\pi)\), giving \(x\in\left(k\pi,\ k\pi+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\) for integers \(k\). Each such interval has length \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\), so the longest interval of decrease is \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\). Hence (C). [Note: the length is \(\pi\) only for \(\cos x\); the double angle halves the period, and with it every monotone interval.]
